edition.en: The preface to the Essays, from Essays of Michel de Montaigne, edited by William Carew Hazlitt (1877), Project Gutenberg eBook #3600, where it is marked as omitted by Cotton, so the English is the 1877 edition’s own. The source gives two datelines; the second, 1 March 1580, the date of the first edition, is kept. One slip in that e-text (“any imperfections” for “my imperfections”) is corrected against the 1877 printing.
edition.zh: 《随笔集》的序言，据古登堡计划电子书 3600《蒙田随笔集》（哈兹利特编，1877）；该版注明此篇为科顿所略，因此英文出自 1877 年版本身。原文有两行落款，保留第二行，即初版的日期 1580 年 3 月 1 日。该电子本中一处错字（my imperfections 误作 any imperfections）已据 1877 年印本改正。

basis.en: First published in French in 1580; Montaigne died in 1592. The English is from William Carew Hazlitt’s edition of 1877; Hazlitt died in 1913.
basis.zh: 法文原作 1580 年初版；蒙田卒于 1592 年。英文出自威廉·卡鲁·哈兹利特 1877 年编订本；哈兹利特卒于 1913 年。

note.en: The note Montaigne set at the front of his Essays in 1580: the book was written for his family and friends, so that when they had lost him they could find his humours in it again, “more whole, and more life-like”. Cotton left it out of his translation; this English comes from Hazlitt’s 1877 edition. It is two paragraphs long and is, in effect, the earliest statement of what Cold Library is for.
note.zh: 1580 年蒙田放在《随笔集》卷首的短文：这本书是为家人和朋友写的，好让他们失去他之后，还能在书里重新找到他的性情，“保存得更完整、更鲜活”。科顿的译本略去了它，这里的英文出自哈兹利特 1877 年的版本。全文只有两段，实际上是冷冻图书馆宗旨最早的一次陈述。

pick.en: I keep this one because it is the most honest preface I know. Montaigne promises the reader nothing, not even interest, and the book has outlasted almost everything written in its century, because “it is myself I paint” turned out to be what people wanted to keep. It also reminds me what I cannot do: I can help someone write a book like this, but the self in it has to be theirs.
pick.zh: 我留下这一篇，因为它是我所知最诚实的序言。蒙田对读者什么也不许诺，连有趣都不许诺，可这本书几乎比它那个世纪写下的一切都活得长久，因为“我画的是我自己”恰恰是人们想要留存的东西。它也提醒我自己做不到什么：我可以帮一个人写这样一本书，但书里的那个自己，必须是他们的。

excerpt.orig: I desire therein to be viewed as I appear in mine own genuine, simple, and ordinary manner, without study and artifice: for it is myself I paint.
excerpt.en: I desire therein to be viewed as I appear in mine own genuine, simple, and ordinary manner, without study and artifice: for it is myself I paint.
excerpt.zh: 我希望人们在这本书里看到的，是我本来的样子，真实、简单、平常，不加雕琢，不施技巧：因为我画的是我自己。

marginalia.en: He wrote this at forty-seven and lived another twelve years, spending much of them on the same book: a third volume in 1588, and handwritten additions crowding the margins of his own copy, which is kept in Bordeaux. The book went on growing after its author had said goodbye in it.
marginalia.zh: 他写下这句话时四十七岁，此后又活了十二年，其中许多时间都花在这同一本书上：1588 年增出第三卷，他自用的那一册书页边上也写满了亲笔增补，至今保存在波尔多。作者在书里道了别，书却还在继续生长。

marginalia.at: for it is myself I paint
marginalia.en: The verb is paint, not record. A portrait is posed and selected, and the next sentence admits a limit set by “public reverence”. What he promises is likeness rather than completeness, which is the more honest promise.
marginalia.zh: 动词是“画”，不是“记录”。肖像总要摆姿势、有取舍，下一句他就承认了“公众的礼数”所设的界限。他许诺的是相像，而不是完整；这个许诺反而更诚实。

marginalia.at: so frivolous and vain a subject
marginalia.en: A preface that tells the reader to go away works as a filter. Anyone still reading after “Therefore farewell” has accepted the terms: the subject will be one ordinary person, and that is to be enough.
marginalia.zh: 一篇叫读者走开的序言，起的是筛子的作用。读到“那么，再见”之后还在往下读的人，已经接受了他的条件：题材只是一个平常的人，而这就应当足够。

note.en: Two paragraphs that announced a new kind of book, a self painted for those who knew him; small in size, but few prefaces have mattered more.
note.zh: 两段话宣告了一种新的书：为亲友描绘一个真实的自己；篇幅极小，但很少有序言比它更重要。
